stories.title: Meta wants your next gadget to be Muse-infused
stories.simple_summary: Meta is sharing the code for Muse (their AI helper) for free so other companies can add it to products like TVs and toasters.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to tech companies and engineers — nothing you need to act on right now, though down the road you might see AI features in everyday gadgets.

stories.title: Sean Parker is rebuilding Stability AI around music
stories.simple_summary: Sean Parker, a music industry figure, is starting a company called Stability AI that works with music labels to create AI music tools.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and music industry people — nothing you need to worry about.

stories.title: Meta open sources code to let you make Muse AI gadgets
stories.simple_summary: Meta released free code so anyone can build their own AI gadgets using Meta's Muse assistant, like smart displays or devices connected to your TV.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mainly for people who like building tech projects — ordinary people don't need to do anything.

stories.title: Apple will limit Mac disk access as AI agents ‘substantially’ increase risk
stories.simple_summary: Apple is adding new safety locks to Macs to prevent AI programs from reading all your personal files, emails, and messages without your clear permission.
stories.why_it_matters: This is good news for Mac owners — it means Apple is being more careful about protecting your privacy from AI programs.

stories.title: Affected by layoffs? Don’t miss this $75 deal for your TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 Expo+ Pass
stories.simple_summary: TechCrunch is offering discounted conference passes for people who lost their jobs.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a business opportunity if you were laid off and want to network — not relevant to most people.

stories.title: Apple says it’s tightening macOS ‘Full Disk Access’ controls due to new risks from AI agents
stories.simple_summary: Apple is making it harder for AI programs to access everything on your Mac computer, because these programs are becoming powerful enough to do damage if they get too much permission.
stories.why_it_matters: If you own a Mac, this means Apple is working to keep AI programs from snooping through your private stuff.

stories.title: OpenAI’s Dot agent is enterprise software that can also order your dinner
stories.simple_summary: OpenAI made a new AI helper called Dots that can do business tasks like handling paperwork or ordering food, but it's designed to feel like work software rather than something friendly and casual.
stories.why_it_matters: This is aimed at businesses and may eventually make office work easier, but most small business owners don't need to switch right now.

stories.title: Call it AI, call it Super Intelligence, only 2% of consumers are buying it
stories.simple_summary: Only 2% of shoppers actually believe in or want AI products, even though the White House and tech companies are pushing them hard and renaming AI as 'super intelligence.'
stories.why_it_matters: Most people aren't rushing to buy AI products yet — so you're not alone if you're skeptical.

stories.title: It’s not AI anymore, it’s ‘super intelligence’ (according to the White House)
stories.simple_summary: President Trump signed an order to officially call AI 'super intelligence' instead of 'artificial intelligence,' and tech leaders promised to make AI safer.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly political news — the name change doesn't actually change how AI works or affects your life.

stories.title: Breaking up (with Elon Musk) is hard to do
stories.simple_summary: Elon Musk and Shivon Zilis, who have four children together, announced their breakup on social media.
stories.why_it_matters: This is celebrity gossip — nothing that affects your business or daily life.

stories.title: TechCrunch Disrupt 2026: Blackstone’s Jas Khaira on building the next generation of AI giants
stories.simple_summary: A leader from the investment company Blackstone will speak at a tech conference about building the next big AI companies.
stories.why_it_matters: This is for investors and tech entrepreneurs — nothing you need to know about.

stories.title: Circuit Breaker Labs hopes to make AI safer for your kids (and you)
stories.simple_summary: A company called Circuit Breaker Labs is testing AI systems to see if they might harm people psychologically before those AI programs are released to the public.
stories.why_it_matters: This is good — someone is checking AI for safety risks — but this work happens behind the scenes before you ever interact with these programs.
